name: accordion
title: Accordion
description: Ruled rows that open. Each row sits on a hand-pulled pencil rule; a hovered row gets a highlighter swipe, and an opened row turns its chevron over, writes a margin brace beside its text and lets the words soak in. Radix behaviour and keyboard support are untouched.

a11y: The WAI-ARIA accordion pattern from Radix: each trigger is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` inside a heading; Enter and Space toggle; ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End move between triggers.
The panel is a `region` labelled by its trigger. Closed panels are removed from the accessibility tree.
The chevron, the rules, the swipe and the brace are aria-hidden and pointer-events: none. State is told by aria-expanded and the turned chevron, not by colour.
Keyboard focus draws a blue felt ring round the row; hover-only decoration never carries meaning. Windows high contrast hides the drawings and uses the browser's own focus ring.
Reduced motion (the OS setting or data-motion="reduced") opens rows at once and shows the brace finished.
Right-to-left layouts mirror the brace and text indent; the chevron is symmetric.
meta.usage:
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/ui/accordion"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="item-1" className="w-full">
      <AccordionItem value="item-1">
        <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Yes. It follows the WAI-ARIA pattern.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
      <AccordionItem value="item-2">
        <AccordionTrigger>Is it drawn by hand?</AccordionTrigger>
        <AccordionContent>Every line.</AccordionContent>
      </AccordionItem>
    </Accordion>
  )
}
